route: Temporary Employment Permit (up to six months in twelve); Employment Permit beyond six months

permit.applies: The institution doing business with the applicant writes the covering letter for a Temporary Employment Permit (Form 25); an Employment Permit is applied for only by an employer, a practising lawyer or an immigration consultant, with the worker outside Zambia
permit.first: For an Employment Permit, the post advertised in two leading newspapers, with the selection outcome, and an employment contract or letter of offer
permit.eligibility: A temporary employment permit is issued to a business visitor staying more than 30 days (at most six months in twelve); an employment permit to a person fitted for the work by qualifications or skill, in work with too few people available in Zambia, or of benefit to Zambia (Class A); the employer may hire an expatriate only for a job on the critical-skills list.

sources.title: Department of Immigration (Zambia), Permit Types
sources.said: An Employment Permit is issued to a foreigner who enters the country to take up employment for a period exceeding six (06) months. It can be extended for periods up to a maximum of 10 years. … All applicants should remain outside Zambia until the permit has been approved. Further, only an Employer, a Practising Lawyer and an Immigration Consult can apply for Employment Permits on behalf of a prospective expatriate. … Employment contract or Letter of offer; … Original Press advertisements which have appeared in two leading newspapers in A5 size. … A Temporary Employment Permit is issued to any business visitor who intends to remain in Zambia for a period exceeding thirty (30) days. The validity of the permit should not exceed six (6) months within a period of twelve (12) months. Requirements for issuance Covering letter from the institution doing business with applicant; Duly completed application form (Form 25); … Requirements for renewal/extension Covering letter from the employer indicating the reasons for extension; Duly completed application form (Form 11); and Prescribed fee.

sources.title: Immigration and Deportation Act, No. 18 of 2010 (the Department of Immigration's copy, linked from zambiaimmigration.gov.zm/publications/legislation/)
sources.said: 28. (1) On application being made in the prescribed manner, the Director-General of Immigration may, in consultation with the Ministry responsible for labour, issue an employment permit to any foreigner outside Zambia who— (a) is not a prohibited immigrant; (b) belongs to class A specified in the First Schedule; … (10) The Director-General of Immigration may issue a temporary employment permit to any business visitor who intends to remain in Zambia for a period in excess of thirty days, except that any period granted under a temporary employment permit shall not exceed six months in any period of twelve months. … FIRST SCHEDULE … Class A Any person who intends for gain to engage in any trade, business, profession, employment or other occupation — (a) for which the person is fitted by virtue of the person's academic or professional qualifications, standard of education, skill and financial resources; (b) in which, having regard to the productivity and efficiency of the persons already engaged therein, there is not already a sufficient number of persons engaged or available in Zambia to meet the requirements of the inhabitants of Zambia; or (c) which is likely to be of benefit to the inhabitants of Zambia generally.

sources.title: Immigration and Deportation (Amendment) Act, No. 19 of 2016 (the Department's copy)
sources.said: 9. The principal Act is amended by the repeal of section twenty-four. 10. Section twenty-eight of the principal Act is amended by— (a) the deletion of subsection (2); and (b) the deletion in subsection (5) of the word "five" and the substitution therefor of the word "ten".

sources.title: Employment Code Act, No. 3 of 2019 (the Department's copy), Division 3.4, Employment of Expatriates
sources.said: 61. (1) Subject to the Immigration and Deportation Act, 2010, an employer shall not— (a) employ, in the name of the employer, an expatriate to engage in work that is not a critical skill under a list prepared under section 65 (1)(d); (b) cause the expatriate to engage in work other than that authorised under the permit issued in accordance with the Immigration and Deportation Act, 2010;
